justifications.functional_suitability: Web Application (SPA) serves online claim submission (R-01) and adjusters (R-02). Incremental claim type migration (R-03) is explicitly supported via the Feature Flag / Routing Service, Claim Management Core bounded contexts, and the Anti-Corruption Layer.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Target R-05 (<2 s screens vs. 5 s mainframe latency) is directly solved using Cache / Read Model Store, In-Memory Cache Layer, Data Synchronization / ETL Service, and asynchronous Azure Service Bus decoupled messaging.
justifications.compatibility: Coexists effectively with On-Premise COBOL/DB2 Mainframe via Anti-Corruption Layer, Mainframe Adapter, and On-Premise Active Directory. However, explicit mechanisms to guarantee respecting the tight 23:00-05:00 nightly batch window constraints are lightly specified.
justifications.usability: UI Presentation Layer provides responsive web interfaces for both Customers/Brokers and Claims Adjusters with optimistic UI updates. However, distinct user journeys or specialized operational tools for adjusters versus external brokers are not distinctly separated.
justifications.reliability: Consistency (R-04) and fault tolerance are robustly handled via Outbox Table & Dispatcher, Azure Service Bus DLQs, Polly Circuit Breakers, and deterministic fallback-to-safe-default routing to the legacy mainframe.
justifications.security: Addresses R-07 via Authentication Client connecting to On-Premise Active Directory for SSO, with Security & Middleware Handler enforcing PII masking and audit correlation. External customer/broker authentication mechanics against AD remain slightly ambiguous.
justifications.maintainability: R-06 (switching back within one day) is thoroughly addressed by the Feature Flag / Routing Service, Circuit Breaker Manager, and Cache Invalidation Publisher. Clean architecture, ACL, and Modular Domain Packages keep coupling low.
justifications.portability: Appropriately targets Azure and on-premise hybrid environments using containerized Azure App Services, standard REST, AMQP, and Azure Service Bus. Azure managed-service dependencies create mild cloud vendor lock-in.

PERF-01.justification: The Read Model Database Engine and In-Memory Cache Store decouple screen reads from mainframe latency. Adjuster screens query pre-synchronized read models directly, satisfying the sub-2-second target regardless of mainframe delays.
sensitivity_points: Data synchronization replication lag directly impacts read model freshness
tradeoffs: Fast read responses traded against eventual consistency of mainframe state

PERF-02.justification: Submissions are buffered asynchronously using Azure Service Bus and the Outbox pattern. While peak load is isolated from the mainframe, explicit rate-limiting or batch-window scheduling controls are not fully detailed.
sensitivity_points: Message queue buffering capacity during peak submission volumes
tradeoffs: Decoupled submission ingestion traded against delayed propagation to legacy core

AVAIL-01.justification: The Outbox Table & Dispatcher and Azure Service Bus buffer incoming submissions while the mainframe is offline. Circuit breakers prevent cascading timeouts, ensuring submissions are preserved and dispatched when the window closes.
sensitivity_points: Outbox table storage capacity and queue durability during extended offline windows
tradeoffs: Continuous online availability traded against deferred legacy backend processing

AVAIL-02.justification: The Outbox Pattern Handler, Resilient Message Handler, and Dead-Letter Queue Manager prevent message loss during transient network failures. However, automated dual-system reconciliation and deduplication logic for half-processed transactions are insufficiently specified.
sensitivity_points: Idempotency handling across legacy DB2 and modern cloud databases
tradeoffs: Reliable message delivery with DLQs traded against manual intervention for complex reconcile failures

MOD-01.justification: The Feature Flag / Routing Service with Consistent Hashing and Cache Invalidation allows rapid rollouts and sub-day switchbacks. Modular Domain Packages isolate new claim logic, while the ACL minimizes mainframe interface changes.
sensitivity_points: Centralized feature flag rule propagation across hybrid routing components
tradeoffs: Dynamic routing flexibility traded against increased routing evaluation overhead

MOD-02.justification: The UI and BFF depend strictly on modern domain APIs rather than legacy contracts. When the mainframe is retired, only the ACL and synchronization layers are decommissioned, leaving the frontend and core intact.
sensitivity_points: Strict adherence to domain encapsulation behind the BFF boundary
tradeoffs: Higher initial architectural indirection traded against zero frontend rewrite on retirement

SEC-01.justification: The architecture includes Active Directory SSO and Security Middleware Handler, but resource-level multi-tenant authorization rules (isolating broker portfolios) are not explicitly detailed, relying mostly on generic middleware.
sensitivity_points: Granular broker claim tenancy enforcement in BFF middleware
tradeoffs: Centralized middleware security checks traded against custom domain authorization logic

SEC-02.justification: Active Directory SSO centralization ensures revoked credentials immediately block new logins. However, token lifetime enforcement and distributed session invalidation across active SPA sessions within 15 minutes are not detailed.
sensitivity_points: JWT and SSO token expiration limits across hybrid boundaries
tradeoffs: Stateless token performance traded against delay in propagating immediate session revocations
